title: MERS-CoV Spike Glycoprotein ELISA Protocol
author: Mustapha Bittaye
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgr6jv9e
materials: Open the Gen5 software, create new experiment using the protocol template (MERS STANDARDISED ELISA_SAMPLE ANALYSIS TEMPLATE) located in this folder (X:\Vaccine\10. MERS-CoV\1. MERS001_Oxford\12.0 Immunology\8. ELISA\Data and analysis\MERS001 STANDARDISED ELISA_SAMPLE ANALYSIS DATA).

steps.title: Prepare Documentation and Plates
steps.instruction: Prepare the administrative records and determine the number of Nunc Immuno ELISA plates needed.

substeps.instruction: Print a new ELISA record sheet (from X:\KEwer\7. ELISA\Templates and protocols).
Assign the next experiment number and fill in required information.
Calculate plate requirements: one plate accommodates 23 samples, an internal control in triplicate, and a standard curve in duplicate.

steps.title: Prepare Spike GP Coating Solution
steps.instruction: Thaw MERS-CoV clamped spike GP (0.5 mg/ml stock at -80 °C) and dilute in DPBS according to the number of plates:

substeps.instruction: 1 plate: 10 µL stock + 4.99 mL DPBS
2 plates: 20 µL stock + 9.98 mL DPBS
3 plates: 30 µL stock + 14.97 mL DPBS
4 plates: 40 µL stock + 19.98 mL DPBS
5 plates: 50 µL stock + 24.95 mL DPBS
6 plates: 60 µL stock + 29.94 mL DPBS

steps.title: Coat and Incubate Plates
steps.instruction: Coat the plates with the prepared MERS-CoV Spike clamped GP (1.0 μg/ml in DPBS).

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µl/well of the coating solution.
Cover plates with clingfilm and store overnight for 18:00:00 at 4 °C.
Record the coating time on the experiment record sheet.

steps.title: Prepare Serum Samples
steps.instruction: Thaw and dilute serum samples for the assay.

substeps.instruction: Thaw required serum samples (up to 23 per plate) at room temperature for at least 01:00:00.
Vortex thawed samples thoroughly.
Dilute samples in casein at 1:500 (5 µL sample in 2495 µL casein) and vortex; ensure a minimum of 5 µL sample is used for all dilutions.

steps.title: Wash and Block Plates
steps.instruction: Remove coating solution and block the plates to prevent non-specific binding.

substeps.instruction: Flick off coating solution into the sink (wear eye protection).
Wash plates 6x in DPBS/T using a handheld plate washer, tapping dry on paper towels between washes.
After the final wash, invert plates, tap firmly, leave on the bench for 2 min, and tap firmly again to remove residual liquid.
Add 100 µL of casein per well to block plates.
Stack plates (with an empty blank plate on top) and incubate for 01:00:00 at room temperature.
Record the blocking time on the experiment sheet.

steps.title: Prepare Standard Curve and Internal Control
steps.instruction: Prepare the two-fold dilution series for the standard curve and the internal control.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1:100 working standards in casein: 6 µL positive standard pool in 594 µL casein (final volume 600 µL). Store at -80 °C.
For 2 plates, prepare a two-fold series in tubes 1-10: Add 520 µL of 1:100 working standard to Tube 1 and 260 µL casein to Tubes 2-10.
Transfer 260 µL from Tube 1 to Tube 2, mix 15 times, and repeat sequentially through Tube 10; discard 260 µL from Tube 10.
Prepare a 1:800 dilution of standard serum pool in casein for internal control (e.g., 25 µL positive standard pool + 175 µL casein per plate).

steps.title: Add Samples and Standards
steps.instruction: Load the diluted samples, standards, and controls into the plates.

substeps.instruction: Flick off blocking solution and tap dry.
Add 50 µL of diluted samples (in triplicate) and blank control (casein only) according to the plate layout.
Add 50 µL of standards sequentially: 1:100, then 1:200, etc.
Add the 1:800 internal control to wells D12, E12, and F12 immediately after the 1:800 standard, then finish the remaining standards.
Cover plates with an empty blank plate and incubate at room temperature for 02:00:00.

steps.title: Secondary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Apply the detection antibody to the plates.

substeps.instruction: Wash plates 6x in DPBS/T using the handheld plate washer as previously described.
Dilute anti-human IgG antibody alkaline phosphatase 1:1000 in casein.
Add 50 µL of detection antibody to each well.
Cover with a blank plate and incubate at room temperature for 01:00:00.

steps.title: Develop the ELISA
steps.instruction: Prepare the substrate and develop the signal.

substeps.instruction: Prepare pNPP substrate (development buffer) at least 00:30:00 prior to use, protecting from light:
1-2 plates: 1 pNPP tablet, 4 mL 5X DEA buffer, 16 mL H2O
3-4 plates: 2 pNPP tablets, 8 mL 5X DEA buffer, 32 mL H2O
5-6 plates: 3 pNPP tablets, 12 mL 5X DEA buffer, 48 mL H2O
Wash plates 6x in DPBS/T using the handheld plate washer.
Add 100 µL development buffer to each well. Add to internal control column (Col 12) immediately after the 1:800 standard column (Col 4), then complete Columns 5-11.

steps.title: Read and Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance and process the results in Excel.

substeps.instruction: Wipe the bottom of the plate dry and place in the plate reader.
Read plate at OD405 starting after 00:10:00; repeat until values fit expected parameters (Internal control: 0.9-1.1; St 1:100: 3.5-3.8; St 1:800: close to internal control; Blank: 0.996).
Export data to Excel and save the Gen5 Experiment and worksheet in the corresponding folder.
Analyze data using the 'ELISA analysis template' (X:\KEwer\7. ELISA\Templates and protocols), completing all blue-shaded fields.
Paste plate layout, data, and parameters (A, B, C, D, and R2) into the 'plate layout and data' sheet.
Identify outliers (high CV) by highlighting in yellow and averaging the remaining two wells of the triplicate.
Assign samples with values > 225 ELISA units as positive.
For samples 'TOO LOW' at 1:100, assign a value of 1 (negative). For samples 'TOO LOW' at 1:500, repeat at 1:100. For samples 'TOO HIGH' at 1:500, repeat at higher dilutions (e.g., 1:1000, 1:2000).
Add all assay parameter data to the designated QC workbook and QC all clinical trial data prior to publication.
